name: Daytona International Speedway
description: The track shape is tri-oval. The turns are banked at 31 degrees and the tri-oval at 18 degrees.

name: Charlotte Motor Speedway
description: The track is tri-oval in shape.Turns are banked at 24 degrees, banking on straightaways is 5 degrees.

name: Texas Motor Speedway
description: Tri-Oval in shape. Turns are banked at 24 degrees, straightaway banked at 5 degrees. Shape is similar to Lowe's Motor Speedway.

name: Phoenix Raceway
description: 5 cornered, off-set tri-oval. Turns 1 and 2 banked at 9 degrees, turns 3 and 4 banked at 11 degrees, straightaways are flat.

name: Bristol Motor Speedway
description: Fastest short track in the nation.Turns are banked at 24-28 degrees. Straightaways are banked at 16 degrees. The infield was originally a football field, in hopes of attracting NFL pre-season games. Most wins,Darrell Waltrip.

name: Dover Motor Speedway
description: The track is oval in shape. It was built around an existing horse racing track. The turns are banked at 24 degrees. The straightaways are banked at 9 degrees. The backstretch grandstand is air conditioned.

name: Talladega Superspeedway
description: Tri-oval in shape. Been called Daytona's "sister track".Turns are banked at 33 degrees,tri-oval banked at 18 degrees, backstretch banked at 2 degrees.

name: Martinsville Speedway
description: The track is oval in shape. Lower portion of turns are concrete. turns are banked at 12 degrees, straightaways are flat. Martinsville is a "charter" NASCAR track and the oldest on the circuit. Originally a dirt surface, it was paved in 1955.

name: South Boston Speedway

name: Richmond Raceway
description: Tri-oval in shape. Turns banked at 14 degrees, frontstretch banked at 8 degrees, backstretch banked at 2 degrees. track was originally a 1/2 mile dirt track. It was paved in 1968 and reconfigured in 1988. Once was known as Strawberry Hill Speedway.

name: Kansas Speedway
description: The track is tri-oval in shape.Turns are banked at 15 degrees, tri-oval is banked at 10.4 degrees, backstretch is banked at 5 degrees.

name: Las Vegas Motor Speedway

name: Michigan International Speedway
description: Tri-Oval in shape. Track was designed by Charlie Moneypenny who designed Daytona. Turns banked at 18 degrees, frontstretch banked at 12 degrees, backstretch banked at 5 degrees.

name: EchoPark Speedway
description: Tri-oval in shape.Currently the fastest track on the circuit.Turns are banked at 24 degrees. Straightaways are banked at 5 degrees. The track was originally oval in shape. It was reconfigured mid-season 1997.

name: Pocono Raceway

description: One of the most unusual  track layouts on the circuit. This tri-oval speedway features three distinct turns with three different radius' and three different degrees of banking. Pocono features the longest straightaway in NASCAR.

name: New Hampshire Motor Speedway
description: Oval in shape. Turns are variably banked at 2 and 7 degrees, straightaways are banked at 1 degree. Built on the site of the historic Bryar Motorsports Park.

name: Darlington Raceway
description: The track is egg shaped, narrower at turns 1 & 2. The first and second turns are banked at 25 degrees. The third and fourth turns are banked at 23 degrees. Straightaways are banked at 2 degrees.First asphalt track on which NASCAR competed.

name: Chicagoland Speedway
description: The track is tri-oval in shape. Turns banked at 18 degrees, tri-oval banked at 11 degrees, backstretch banked at 5 degrees.

name: Langley Speedway
